record.paper_title: Initial state fluctuations and final state correlations: Status and open questions
record.context_brief: Future measurements for non-flow and mode mixing
record.original_question: What future measurements of two-particle-correlation factorization, trigger and associated pseudorapidity dependence, and flow coefficients measured relative to event planes of different harmonic order should be used to distinguish bulk anisotropies from non-flow effects, study flow fluctuations, and probe hydrodynamic mode mixing?

evidence.quote:
The extensive
factorization tests of two-particle correlations (Vn∆) over a large range of trigger and
associated particle transverse momentum as carried out by the LHC collaborations are
useful to distinguish bulk anisotropies from other/non-flow contributions, as well as
to study flow fluctuations. Similar analyses can be done in the space of trigger and
associated pseudorapidity. Measurements of vn coefficients with respect to an event
plane of different order Ψm with m 6= n are sensitive to the hydrodynamic response and
give insights about mode-mixing.

artifact.status_search_result: The question proposes a measurement program rather than a precise mathematical conjecture. Subsequent LHC analyses (ATLAS, CMS, ALICE) have performed factorization-breaking measurements of V_{nΔ}(p_T^a, p_T^t), pseudorapidity-dependent factorization studies, and event-plane correlations sensitive to mode mixing, but the program as a whole (fully disentangling non-flow, fluctuations, and mode mixing) remains an active area without a definitive resolution.

status_evidence.title: Initial state fluctuations and final state correlations
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses future measurements to distinguish bulk anisotropies from non-flow and probe mode mixing.
status_evidence.claim: The proposed measurements are stated as open future directions.
